text:
Researchers have unveiled a simple new way to make powerful artificial intelligence models fast and lightweight enough for everyday use by millions of people [P3_p1_c02][P3_p1_c03]. 

Training high-performing machine learning models often requires massive computing power and cumbersome ensembles of multiple models [P3_p1_c02][P3_p1_c03]. While these large models extract great structure from data, they are too expensive to deploy to a large number of users [P3_p1_c02][P3_p1_c03]. 

To solve this, researchers developed a technique called distillation [P3_p1_c03][P3_p2_c04]. Much like biological insects that have a larval form to gather energy and an adult form built for travel, artificial intelligence can use a cumbersome model for training and a small model for deployment [P3_p1_c03]. Distillation transfers the knowledge from a large ensemble into a single, compact model by using a higher temperature on the final output probabilities to preserve valuable similarity structure, such as learning which images or sounds resemble one another [P3_p1_c02][P3_p2_c04]. 

In key results, this approach successfully improved a heavily used commercial speech recognition system [P3_p1_c02]. More than 80% of the accuracy improvement gained by an ensemble of 10 models was successfully transferred to a single distilled model [P3_p5_c02]. This breakthrough matters because it bridges the gap between heavy-duty AI training and real-world deployment, making advanced technology significantly cheaper and faster to run for everyday users [P3_p1_c02][P3_p1_c03].
